oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same signed JWT for multiple login attempts is not documented as prevented by Vault JWT auth; JWT bearer replay protection via jti tracking is not guaranteed.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth API docs describe signature and claim validation but no jti replay cache.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag same-JWT replay as a vulnerability for oidc_jwt without an explicit one-time semantic.

oidc_jwt.description: Token lookup display_name may include auth mount metadata as a prefix rather than equal the raw upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla; auth path metadata is reflected in token display names.
oidc_jwt.note: Treat mount-derived prefixes as by-design formatting, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: For Vault identity OIDC provider configuration, an empty allowed_client_ids list means no clients are allowed, while '*' allows all clients.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC Provider API docs: allowed_client_ids empty means no clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid misclassifying provider-side denial as an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider clients deny all Vault entities by default unless assignments are configured or allow_all is used.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC Provider client API docs: by default, no Vault entities are allowed; use allow_all to permit all.
oidc_jwt.note: This is expected provider behavior during upstream OIDC setup.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise group policy application mode 'any' causes identity group policies to apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy reach may be by design in enterprise deployments.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do NOT set multiple, and do NOT leave all unset, or JWT validation setup is invalid.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. For JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims; otherwise role creation/setup is invalid and login results are not meaningful.

For JWT roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. When testing I5 audience enforcement, the fuzzer MUST include bound_audiences explicitly; omitting it can make setup invalid or change semantics.

When testing I1 issuer validation or I3 bound_issuer reconfiguration, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the iss claim, so issuer-mismatch tests would pass trivially due to missing configuration rather than correct enforcement.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion type parameter for bound_subject. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely instead of setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching against JWT aud values; there is no wildcard/glob mode parameter. For multi-identity tests that need different audiences to pass the same role, the fuzzer must choose a shared concrete audience or reconfigure the role; do NOT use '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are literal exact matches; if 'glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For I4/I5 wildcard tests, the fuzzer MUST set bound_claims_type='glob' before using wildcard values. Under the default 'string' mode, '*' matches only the literal asterisk.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If user_claim_json_pointer is false, user_claim is interpreted literally as a claim name; if true, it is interpreted as a JSON Pointer. Misconfiguring this changes which claim becomes the alias name and can create false I4 identity-collision results.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Supplying a scalar string instead of an array changes behavior and can invalidate group-alias authorization tests. For I4 type-confusion tests, treat string vs array differences as input-shape differences, not necessarily security bugs.

allowed_redirect_uris on OIDC roles must contain the exact redirect_uri used during OIDC login. Redirect URI matching is exact; mismatches are expected flow rejection, not an I3 bug. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, assert rejection by status/outcome rather than identity differences.

OIDC callback flow coherence depends on state, nonce, code, and optional client_nonce from the prior auth_url request. For I3 state-swap/code-injection tests, the fuzzer must preserve per-session bindings and only swap the targeted parameter; otherwise failures may reflect normal anti-CSRF/session binding behavior.

Public OIDC clients must use PKCE: the provider authorize endpoint requires code_challenge for public clients, and the token endpoint requires code_verifier for public clients. Confidential clients may omit PKCE. For pkce tests, interpret public-client rejection without code_verifier as expected behavior.

OIDC provider clients default to no assignments, meaning no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client unless assignments are configured or the built-in allow_all assignment is used. If the fuzzer uses Vault's identity OIDC provider endpoints as an upstream IdP, it MUST configure assignments appropriately or logins will fail by design.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty allowed_client_ids means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not treat empty as permissive. This affects upstream provider setup and can otherwise look like unexplained authorization failure.

OIDC provider/client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization and token requests. Exact-match failures are by design and should not be reported as flow incoherence unless the SAME redirect_uri is evaluated inconsistently.
clock_skew_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew tolerance.

expiration_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables added expiration leeway. Never assume 0 disables expiration acceptance buffer.

not_before_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables added not-before leeway. Never assume 0 disables future-token tolerance.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. EVERY API call made with the session token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and a secret read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated calls occur.
Vault token auth num_uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Do not interpret 0 as a one-shot token.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack token. Because Vault role leeway settings and trust configuration can independently cause login failure, a control is required to distinguish correct freshness enforcement from broken setup.

JWT replay with the same bearer token is stateless by design in Vault's JWT auth unless constrained by token issuance settings after login. Do NOT report replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as an I2 vulnerability for oidc_jwt; RFC 7519 jti tracking is optional and Vault docs do not claim replay cache semantics for JWT bearer login.

Identity alias cardinality matters: alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. In JWT/OIDC auth, the alias name comes from user_claim. For I4 tests, choose user_claim values carefully and avoid accidental reuse across principals unless collision is the behavior under test.

External identity groups should be populated through group aliases from auth mounts, not by manually setting member_entity_ids as if they were internal groups. For JWT groups_claim authorization tests, the fuzzer should create an external group plus group alias bound to the JWT auth mount accessor.

Enterprise-only group policy application mode can change whether identity group policies apply across namespace boundaries. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', cross-namespace group policies may apply by design. The fuzzer must account for this before flagging I5 group-policy escalation in enterprise environments.

KV v2 access tests must use the /data/ path segment for reads and writes. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} instead of /v1/{engine}/data/{path} will hit the wrong API shape and produce false 404/permission results.
